title: Practice Exam 8
description: An additional full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam.

questions.question: A driver is following you too closely (tailgating). What is the safest response?
choices: Increase your following distance ahead and, if safe, move over to let them pass
Brake hard to warn the tailgater to back off
Speed up to put distance between you
Stay in your lane and ignore the tailgater
questions.explanation: If tailgated, leave more room ahead so you can brake gradually, and allow the other driver to pass when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing a school building or grounds while children are present, what is the maximum speed (where no lower limit is posted)?
choices: 25 mph
15 mph
35 mph
20 mph
questions.explanation: Near a school with children present, the limit is 25 mph (and as low as 15 mph in some posted zones). Always slow down and watch for children.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: After parking your vehicle on any slope, what should you always do in addition to turning your wheels?
choices: Set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear for a manual)
Leave the transmission in neutral with the brake off
Turn the engine off and leave it in neutral only
Leave the vehicle in drive with the parking brake off
questions.explanation: On any hill, set the parking brake and leave an automatic in 'Park' or a manual in gear as a backup to the turned wheels.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on a Hill

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a business or residential district when no other limit is posted?
choices: 25 mph
30 mph
20 mph
35 mph
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in business and residential districts is 25 mph unless signs say otherwise.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: What does a broken (dashed) white line between lanes indicate?
choices: You may change lanes across it when it is safe
Lane changes are prohibited across it
Traffic flows in opposite directions on each side
You must stop before crossing it
questions.explanation: A broken white line separates lanes moving in the same direction and means you may cross it to change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: You and an oncoming vehicle both arrive at a narrow one-lane bridge at about the same time, but the other vehicle is already partly on the bridge. Who should yield?
choices: You should yield to the vehicle already on the bridge
The vehicle on the bridge must back up for you
Whoever honks first has the right of way
Both should proceed slowly onto the bridge together
questions.explanation: When a road or bridge is too narrow for two vehicles, the driver who has not yet entered should yield to the vehicle already on it.

questions.question: What does a red-and-white sign reading 'DO NOT ENTER' mean?
choices: You may not enter the roadway from your direction
The road is closed only to trucks
Enter slowly and yield to traffic
No parking is allowed beyond this point
questions.explanation: A 'DO NOT ENTER' sign (red and white) marks a roadway you cannot enter, such as an exit ramp or one-way street going the other way.

questions.question: A pedestrian who is blind may signal that they do not intend to cross by:
choices: Pulling in their white cane and stepping back from the curb
Waving their cane in a circle
Tapping the cane three times
Crossing immediately
questions.explanation: When a blind pedestrian pulls in their cane and steps away from the curb, it generally indicates they are not going to cross, and you may proceed with caution.

questions.question: When you enter a school zone and the speed limit sign reads 25 mph, this limit applies:
choices: When children are present or as otherwise indicated by posted hours
Only on weekends
At all hours of every day permanently
Only when a crossing guard is present
questions.explanation: The 25 mph school zone speed generally applies when children are present, or during the hours posted on the sign.

questions.question: A yellow diamond sign with a bicycle symbol means what?
choices: Watch for bicyclists who may be crossing or sharing the road
Bicycles are prohibited on this road
A bicycle repair shop is ahead
A bike lane ends here
questions.explanation: The bicycle warning sign alerts drivers that bicyclists may be present; share the road and watch for them. A prohibition would use a red circle and slash instead.

questions.question: What does a yellow diamond sign with a 'T' symbol indicate?
choices: The road you are on ends ahead at a T-intersection
A truck route turns here
A toll booth is ahead
A tunnel is ahead
questions.explanation: The 'T' warning sign means the road you are traveling on ends ahead and you must turn right or left onto the crossing road.

questions.question: After completing a lane change or turn, you notice your turn signal is still blinking. What should you do?
choices: Turn it off so you do not mislead other drivers
Leave it on until you reach your destination
Switch to your hazard lights instead
Leave it on; it will cancel on its own eventually
questions.explanation: A signal left blinking can mislead other drivers about your intentions, so you should turn it off once your maneuver is complete.

questions.question: Even for drivers 18 and older, using a hands-free phone while driving is still risky because:
choices: It causes cognitive distraction that takes your mind off driving
It is illegal for all adults
It always takes both hands off the wheel
It damages the vehicle's electronics
questions.explanation: Hands-free conversation still creates cognitive distraction, diverting mental attention away from driving even though your hands stay on the wheel.

questions.question: What does a steady green arrow pointing left at a signal mean?
choices: You have a protected left turn and oncoming traffic is stopped
You must yield to oncoming traffic before turning left
Left turns are prohibited
You may turn left only after the arrow turns yellow
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow means the turn is protected: oncoming traffic faces a red light, so you may turn in that direction safely.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: On a multi-lane freeway, what is the far-left lane primarily intended for?
choices: Passing and faster-moving traffic
Slow-moving vehicles and trucks
Vehicles preparing to exit on the right
Vehicles that have broken down
questions.explanation: The far-left lane is meant for passing and faster traffic; slower drivers should keep to the right.

questions.question: Before taking an over-the-counter cold or allergy medicine and then driving, you should:
choices: Read the label for warnings about drowsiness or impairment
Take a double dose so it wears off faster
Assume it is safe because no prescription is needed
Drink coffee with it to stay alert
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter cold, allergy, and sleep aids cause drowsiness and can impair driving. Always check the label warnings before getting behind the wheel.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: On a long downgrade, how should you manage your speed with a heavy load or while towing?
choices: Shift to a lower gear before the descent so the engine helps control speed and brakes don't overheat
Coast in neutral to save fuel
Ride the brakes continuously the whole way down
Increase speed to get down the hill faster
questions.explanation: Downshifting before a long downgrade uses engine braking to control speed and prevents brake fade from overheating; coasting in neutral is unsafe and illegal.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — California's Basic Speed Law

questions.question: When driving near bicyclists at night, you should be aware that:
choices: Bicyclists can be hard to see, so use extra caution and watch for reflectors and lights
Bicyclists are not allowed to ride at night
Bicyclists must ride only on sidewalks after dark
Your headlights make bicyclists fully visible
questions.explanation: At night bicyclists are harder to see, so drive with extra caution and look for their required lights and reflectors.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: What do the two solid parallel (double white) lines bordering a carpool/HOV lane mean?
choices: You may not cross them; enter or exit only at designated openings
You may cross them at any time to enter the lane
They mark the freeway shoulder
They indicate a lane that is closed to all traffic
questions.explanation: Never change lanes across the double solid white lines bordering a carpool/HOV lane; enter or exit only where the line is broken.

questions.question: How does the number of drinks consumed relate to your blood alcohol concentration?
choices: The more you drink in a given time, the higher your BAC rises
BAC stays the same no matter how much you drink
BAC depends only on the type of alcohol, not the amount
BAC drops as you drink more
questions.explanation: BAC rises as more alcohol enters the bloodstream faster than the liver can remove it. Drinking more in a short time raises BAC further.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: Which statement about distracted driving is true?
choices: A driver can cause a collision even during a brief glance away from the road
Distraction is only dangerous on the freeway
Experienced drivers are immune to distraction
Only texting counts as distracted driving
questions.explanation: Even a momentary glance away can lead to a crash. Many activities besides texting — eating, grooming, adjusting controls — divert attention and create risk.

questions.question: You are on a divided highway and an emergency vehicle approaches from the opposite side, behind a median or barrier. What should you do?
choices: You generally do not need to pull over, since the median separates you, but stay alert
Always come to a full stop on your side
Cross the median to make room
Speed up to clear the area
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is on the other side of a divided highway separated by a barrier, you usually do not need to pull over, but remain cautious.

questions.question: You are waiting to make a left turn when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren. What should you do?
choices: Stop and let it pass, then complete your turn when it is safe
Complete your turn quickly before it arrives
Continue into the intersection and stop there
Back up to clear the intersection
questions.explanation: Yield to the emergency vehicle by stopping and waiting until it passes before completing your left turn.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to avoid the temptation to check your phone while driving?
choices: Silence it or put it out of reach before you start driving
Keep it in your lap so you can glance quickly
Mount it where you can read every notification
Answer messages only at stop signs
questions.explanation: Putting your phone on silent or out of reach removes the temptation to respond, helping you keep your full attention on driving.

questions.question: Under California's 'Move Over, Slow Down' law, what must you do when approaching a stopped emergency, tow, or Caltrans vehicle with flashing amber or emergency lights?
choices: Move over to another lane if safe, or slow down if you cannot move over
Stop completely behind the vehicle until it leaves
Maintain your speed and stay in your lane
Honk to alert the workers before passing
questions.explanation: The Move Over, Slow Down law requires you to change lanes away from the stopped vehicle when safe, or slow down if you cannot.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Move Over, Slow Down Law

questions.question: You are driving on a divided highway with a raised median when a school bus on the opposite side stops with red lights flashing. You should:
choices: Continue driving with caution; you are not required to stop
Stop until the lights stop flashing
Stop only if you see children
Pull over and wait two minutes
questions.explanation: On a divided highway separated by a median, traffic moving in the opposite direction of a stopped school bus does not have to stop.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road / School Buses

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in a school zone when children are present is:
choices: 25 mph
35 mph
15 mph
45 mph
questions.explanation: The school zone speed limit is 25 mph when children are present, though some zones post lower limits.

questions.question: When two cars reach an intersection with a non-working (completely dark) signal at the same time, who yields?
choices: Treat it as an all-way stop; the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right
The first car to honk has the right-of-way
Both drivers may proceed at the same time
The faster-moving vehicle goes first
questions.explanation: A dark signal is treated as an all-way stop. When two vehicles arrive together, the driver on the left yields to the one on the right.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, in which direction should you drive and to whom do you yield?
choices: Drive counterclockwise and yield to traffic already in the roundabout
Drive clockwise and yield to traffic about to enter
Drive counterclockwise and you have the right of way over circulating traffic
Drive clockwise and yield only to pedestrians
questions.explanation: In a roundabout you travel counterclockwise around the central island and must yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout before entering.

questions.question: How close to a fire hydrant are you allowed to park?
choices: No closer than 15 feet
No closer than 5 feet
No closer than 10 feet
No closer than 25 feet
questions.explanation: You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking (Where It Is Illegal to Park)

questions.question: You see a ramp meter (a small traffic signal) on a freeway on-ramp. What does it do?
choices: It controls the rate vehicles enter the freeway, releasing one car per green
It signals that the freeway is closed ahead
It marks the carpool-only entrance
It tells you to stop and park until traffic clears
questions.explanation: Ramp meters are signals that release vehicles onto the freeway one at a time to smooth the flow of merging traffic and reduce congestion.

questions.question: A blind pedestrian carrying a white cane or using a guide dog is waiting at a corner. What is the correct action?
choices: Stop and yield the right of way, allowing them to cross
Drive past quickly so you do not delay them
Honk twice to signal it is safe for them to cross
Wait only if a traffic signal requires you to stop
questions.explanation: You must always yield the right of way to a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog. Avoid honking, as it can confuse them.

questions.question: Why is weaving in and out of lanes to get ahead in traffic discouraged?
choices: It is dangerous and rarely saves significant time
It is the fastest legal way to travel
It is only unsafe at night
It is required to keep traffic flowing
questions.explanation: Frequent lane changes to weave through traffic increase the risk of a collision and usually save little or no time.

questions.question: What is the best way to make sure everyone gets home safely from a party where alcohol is served?
choices: Arrange a designated sober driver in advance
Have each person drink water before leaving
Wait 30 minutes after the last drink
Let the person who drank the least drive
questions.explanation: Choosing a designated driver who will not drink at all is the safest plan. Others may also use a rideshare, taxi, or public transit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: What does a 'WALK' signal or walking-person symbol mean for a pedestrian?
choices: It is legal to start crossing the street in the marked crosswalk
Pedestrians must wait; vehicles have the right-of-way
Pedestrians may cross only if running
The crosswalk is permanently closed
questions.explanation: A steady 'WALK' or walking-person signal tells pedestrians they may begin crossing. A flashing 'DON'T WALK' or upraised hand means do not start crossing.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance the handbook recommends under good driving conditions?
choices: At least three seconds behind the vehicle ahead
At least one car length per 10 mph
At least one second behind the vehicle ahead
At least 50 feet at any speed
questions.explanation: Use the three-second rule: leave at least three seconds of following distance behind the vehicle ahead in good conditions.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Distance (Three-Second Rule)
